main_body: two-story half-timbered tavern building with tiled roof
top_band: orange-brown tiled roof slope across rows 0-43 (with chimney top opening visible at rows 8-10)
evidence: The main body is a building with a large foreshortened roof slope (rows 0-43) above a two-story front wall face (rows 44-94). Row 43-44 forms a distinct eave edge with a cast shadow on rows 44-45 of the plaster wall, the doorway is recessed into its frame, and the chimney shows its top opening.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul house references on the left, the candidate's roof tiles are regular rectangular blocks repeated uniformly rather than organic, varied tile scallops with deep contrast, and the outer roof edges use a stark near-black staircase outline. The plaster wall has light speckle, and the wood framing and chimney are flatter and simpler than the reference brickwork and timber.
